analysis: The only security-relevant code change is in coordinator/api/accounts/erasure/handlers.go (hunk @@ -243,6 +243,8). After a successful account-erasure cancellation, the handler now calls s.access.InvalidateAllAPIKeyCache(). This drops cached API-key refusals for keys that the erasure request had revoked. Those keys become live again on cancel, so the call removes a stale-denial availability problem. It falls after the error return, so a failed cancel does not trigger it. It does not widen authorization. It relates to T-059 (account erasure / TB-006) and to the revocation-cache freshness theme. I could not see the cancel handler's authorization (admin vs. account owner, actor attribution) or the symmetric invalidation on the erasure-request / revoke path. The next pass should confirm that the revoke path also calls InvalidateAllAPIKeyCache, so a revoked key cannot stay cached as valid. It should also check whether the global invalidation could be triggered repeatedly by an authorized caller for cache-stampede DoS. Neither can be judged from this diff. CHANGELOG.md (lines 1012-1778, units 15-17) is documentation only; it covers GPT-OSS perf, HF downloads, SSD prefix checkpoints, profiler (T-051), and runtime manifest changes. No code or trust-boundary behavior changes there, and it does not alter threat-model assumptions. The unit for 3f05d63e5c3b6022:0 carried only metadata, with no content or mode change.
